<thought>Based on the isotopic envelope: a strong M+1 peak (~16 % of base) matches the expected 13C contribution for ~15 carbons, indicating carbon. A distinct M+2 peak (~4–5 % of base) aligns with the natural abundance of 34S (~4.2 %), confirming sulfur. No other characteristic patterns (e.g., Cl, Br) are evident. Therefore the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and sulfur.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'S']</final_answer>
